name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Scenic hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with pine forests, colonial architecture, lakes, waterfalls, and vibrant Khasi culture. Main gateway for the region.
facts: Capital of Meghalaya and HQ of East Khasi Hills
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong on Shillong Peak
Nearest airport Umroi; major access via Guwahati

name: Jowai
description: District headquarters of West Jaintia Hills at about 1,380 m elevation, cultural and commercial hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Gateway for the district’s waterfalls, monoliths, lakes and the Dawki circuit; known for local markets and traditional crafts.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district since 2012
Base for Krang Suri, Nartiang and Dawki circuits

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning multi-tiered waterfall near Amlarem with vivid turquoise pool amid limestone cliffs and dense forest. One of Meghalaya’s most photogenic falls; short trek to the base where swimming with life jackets is possible.
facts: Near Amlarem, about 30–90 km from Shillong via Jowai
Entry fee applies; life jackets available
Best early morning for light and fewer crowds

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megalithic stones in the Khasi-Jaintia region, north of Nartiang market. Menhirs and dolmens erected 16th–19th centuries by Jaintia kings and clans; tallest over 8 m, protected as national monument.
facts: Asia’s densest megalithic collection in one area

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti), one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Located in Nartiang village, former summer capital of Jaintia kings; major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.
facts: Shakti as Jayanti, Bhairava as Kamadishwar

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (Pung Sajar Nangli) beside NH-6 near Mukhla village, about 10 km from Jowai. Surrounded by pine forests; popular for picnics, boating and photography with a distinctive red boathouse.
facts: Man-made lake with legend of Sajar Nangli
About 10 km from Jowai on NH-6
Popular local picnic and boating spot

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town and stretch of the Umngot River famed for crystal-clear turquoise waters where boats appear to float in air. Historic 1932 suspension bridge; major boating and photography destination near the India-Bangladesh border.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River, preferred quieter base for clear-water boating, kayaking, cliff-jumping, camping and homestays. Less crowded alternative to the main Dawki ghat.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong–Jowai road, often compared to Elephant Falls. Accessible via a short walk across an arch bridge over paddy fields with views of the valley.

name: Thlu Muwi
description: Historic granite stone-slab bridge on the Jowai–Dawki road, built under Jaintia kings for monsoon travel. Adjacent Muwi Waterfall; rare example of traditional megalithic bridge engineering.
facts: About 15–16 km from Jowai on Dawki road
Built by Mar Phalyngki and Luh Lamare

name: Ialong Park
description: Eco-park about 8 km from Jowai with sacred grove and panoramic views over Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Developed for tourism with trails, viewpoints and picnic facilities.
facts: Popular local picnic and walk spot

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Riverside picnic and heritage site on the Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning “golden flower”. Site linked to freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah; features suspension bridge, fish sanctuary and local gatherings.
facts: Linked to Kiang Nangbah freedom struggle

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered waterfall with turquoise pool near Shkentalang village, about 22 km from Jowai. Hidden gem requiring a short hike; less crowded alternative with clear pools and forested setting.
facts: Short hike from parking near Shkentalang

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Iconic hill station and sub-divisional town in East Khasi Hills on the southern Khasi plateau at about 1,430 m elevation. Famous as one of the wettest places on Earth, with dramatic cliffs, waterfalls, caves, living root bridges and views over the Bangladesh plains. Traditional capital of the Sohra Hima.
facts: Record rainfall exceeding 26,000 mm in a year historically
Gateway to Nohkalikai Falls, Mawsmai Cave and root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: India’s tallest plunge waterfall near Sohra, dropping about 340 m in a single cascade from the plateau edge into a turquoise pool below. Dramatic limestone cliffs and forested gorge; best viewed from the cliff-top plaza. Associated with a local Khasi legend.
facts: Best flow during monsoon into early winter
One of Meghalaya’s most photographed falls

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew. Cascades through fern-covered rocky dells; the lowest tier is the most spectacular. Easily accessible and popular for short visits.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city centre
Named after a former elephant-shaped rock

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located roughly 10 km south of Shillong. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills and, on clear days, the plains. Sacred to the Khasi people as the abode of the deity Lei Shyllong; also hosts an Air Force radar station.
facts: Sacred site for Khasi deity Lei Shyllong
Panoramic views of city and countryside

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Remote Khasi village near the Bangladesh border, widely recognised as one of Asia’s cleanest villages. Features neat thatched and wooden houses, living root bridge nearby, bamboo skywalk, and community-led eco-tourism with high literacy and strict cleanliness norms.
facts: Nearby single living root bridge at Riwai

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees across a stream over generations. Requires a steep descent of roughly 3,000–3,500 steps from Tyrna; surrounded by rainforest, pools and further trails to Rainbow Falls.
facts: Only double-decker living root bridge of its kind
About 15 km from Sohra; trek starts at Tyrna
Further trail to Rainbow Falls possible

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon and viewpoint near Smit village, about 25 km from Shillong. Meaning “end of hills” in Khasi; offers sweeping views of layered green ridges and deep valleys. Optional steep staircase descent toward villages below.
facts: Name means end of the hills

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient protected sacred grove near Mawphlang village, about 25 km from Shillong. Preserved by Khasi tradition as the abode of a local deity; rich biodiversity with ancient trees, monoliths and a strict rule against removing anything from the forest.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong on Shillong-Sohra road
Strict rule: nothing may be removed

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra, with a short lit section featuring stalactites, stalagmites and fossil impressions. One of the first caves developed for tourists in Meghalaya; easy entry for most visitors.
facts: Lit for visitors; entry fee applies
First show cave in the region

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall plunging about 315 m over limestone cliffs near Mawsmai, south of Sohra. Dramatic multi-stream cascade best seen in monsoon; viewpoint offers sweeping vistas toward the plains.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters Falls
About 1 km south of Mawsmai village
